title: What mechanics do
d: Auto mechanics diagnose, maintain, and repair cars and light trucks: engines, transmissions, brakes, suspension, electrical, and now hybrids and EVs. Modern wor
description: Auto mechanics diagnose, maintain, and repair cars and light trucks: engines, transmissions, brakes, suspension, electrical, and now hybrids and EVs. Modern work is half computer diagnostics, half wrenches. ASE certification is the industry credential.

title: Essential tools
d: Socket sets (metric and SAE), combination wrenches, screwdrivers, pliers, torque wrench, breaker bar, jack and jack stands, multimeter, OBD-II scanner, and a ro
description: Socket sets (metric and SAE), combination wrenches, screwdrivers, pliers, torque wrench, breaker bar, jack and jack stands, multimeter, OBD-II scanner, and a rolling tool chest. Pros add: oscilloscope, smoke machine, and specialty pullers.

title: Key skills
d: OBD-II diagnostics and live data interpretation, brake jobs, suspension work, electrical troubleshooting (the hardest skill), timing components, and fluid servi
description: OBD-II diagnostics and live data interpretation, brake jobs, suspension work, electrical troubleshooting (the hardest skill), timing components, and fluid services. Diagnostic ability — finding the real fault — is what earns top pay.

title: Safety essentials
d: Jack stands every time — never trust a jack alone. Eye protection under cars. Hot fluids burn: let things cool. Battery safety: disconnect negative first. Hybri
description: Jack stands every time — never trust a jack alone. Eye protection under cars. Hot fluids burn: let things cool. Battery safety: disconnect negative first. Hybrid/EV high voltage requires special training and insulated tools.

title: Getting started

description: Trade school or community college automotive programs, then apprentice at a shop or dealer. ASE certifications stack up by specialty. Start with maintenance (brakes, oil, tires) and grow into diagnostics.

description: Verify the complaint yourself before touching anything. Fix the cause, not the code — codes point, they do not convict. Torque wheels and critical fasteners. Document everything with photos. Road-test every repair.
